[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guide defines the process for adopting the architecture pipeline (GUID-GOV-PROC-010) on existing projects that were not born from the pipeline. It provides a structured approach for assessing alignment gaps, mapping existing artifacts to their pipeline equivalents, and executing a prioritized backfill plan to bring pre-existing codebases into pipeline compliance.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Accelerates adoption** — teams with existing code and partial documentation can adopt the pipeline without starting from scratch
- **Preserves existing work** — maps current artifacts to pipeline stages so that prior effort is reused rather than discarded
- **Enables incremental compliance** — projects can adopt one stage at a time, starting from the highest-impact gap
- **Unlocks traceability** — once adopted, every implementation issue traces back to a requirement, ADR, and bounded context
- **Standardizes fleet posture** — enables enterprise-wide compliance measurement and fleet health dashboards
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Primary Audience**: Tech Leads and Solution Architects bringing existing projects into pipeline compliance
- **Secondary Audience**: Engineering teams executing backfill tasks within an adoption plan
- **Stakeholders**: Engineering Managers (effort estimation), Enterprise Architecture (compliance tracking), Product Owners (backlog prioritization)

- Existing projects with code but no canonical architecture documentation

page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

- Most Gainwell projects predate the architecture pipeline — they have code, tests, and documentation, but not in the canonical pipeline format
- Enterprise compliance tracking requires a uniform baseline across all projects, regardless of when they started
- Teams requesting architecture review board (CRB/ARB) submissions need pipeline-formatted artifacts even for existing systems
- Merger and acquisition activity introduces projects with entirely different governance practices
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#strategic-alignment]

#### Strategic Alignment

- Supports the Enterprise Architecture Practice mandate for traceable, BDD-driven architecture
- Enables fleet-wide compliance dashboards by bringing all projects to a measurable baseline
- Aligns with the shift-left governance strategy — retroactive traceability uncovers design gaps before they become production incidents
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#problem-statement]

#### Problem Statement

The architecture pipeline (GUID-GOV-PROC-010) defines the gold-standard path from discovery to implementation. However, the pipeline assumes a greenfield starting point — or at least a project that was bootstrapped from the enterprise template. Existing projects face a gap: they have artifacts that carry architectural intent, but those artifacts are not in canonical format, not traceable, and not connected to the pipeline's quality gates.

The `/eap-sdd-adopt` command in the [eap-bootstrap template](https://github.com/mygainwell/eap-bootstrap) automates the gap assessment and backfill plan generation, but projects that have not yet applied the bootstrap template layer need a process-level guide — this document — to understand what adoption entails and how to begin.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#current-state]

#### Current State

Most existing projects exhibit one of these patterns:

| Pattern | Description | Prevalence |
|---------|-------------|------------|
| **Code-only** | Production code with tests, CI/CD, but no architecture documentation | Common in small services |
| **Informal architecture** | README "Architecture" section, ad-hoc diagrams, scattered design docs | Most mid-size projects |
| **Partial pipeline** | Some canonical artifacts (ADRs, glossary) but missing BDD specs or traceability | Early pipeline adopters |
| **Foreign governance** | Architecture artifacts from another framework (TOGAF, SAFe, vendor-specific) | M&A projects |
| **Documentation debt** | Architecture decisions were made verbally or in Confluence/Slack, never codified | Legacy projects |
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#future-state]

#### Future State

After adoption, a project achieves:

- All 11 pipeline stages assessed and either satisfied or explicitly waived
- Existing artifacts transformed into canonical format and stored in standard locations
- BDD feature files in `docs/requirements/functional/` and `docs/requirements/non-functional/`
- Traceable ADRs in `docs/decisions/` with canonical metadata
- Compliance score ≥ 70% (threshold for "pipeline-adopted" status)
- Ability to run `/eap-sdd-health-check` for ongoing integrity validation

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#what-gets-applied]

#### What Gets Applied

The bootstrap template layer adds or updates the following:

| Directory / File | Purpose | Overwrites Existing? |
|-----------------|---------|---------------------|
| `.claude/` | Claude Code commands, skills, settings | No — merges |
| `.github/prompts/` | Copilot workflow prompts | No — additive |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Copilot workspace instructions | Yes — canonical source |
| `.vscode/settings.json` | Shared editor settings | Yes — canonical source |
| `.vscode/mcp.json` | MCP server configuration | Yes — canonical source |
| `onboarding/` | Platform setup scripts | No — additive |
| `Taskfile.yml` | Task runner orchestrator | No — only if missing |
| `.project.yml` | Project configuration | No — only if missing |
| `docs/` structure | Canonical documentation directories | No — creates missing dirs only |
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#how-to-apply]

#### How to Apply

1. **Add the template remote** (if not already a fork):

   ```bash
   git remote add eap-bootstrap https://github.com/mygainwell/eap-bootstrap.git
   git fetch eap-bootstrap main
   ```

2. **Cherry-pick the template layer** using the sync command:

   ```bash
   # From within the project, after bootstrap is available:
   /eap-bootstrap-sync
   ```

   Or manually copy the template directories listed above, preserving any project-specific customizations in `.claude/commands/` and `.github/prompts/`.

3. **Verify the template** is functional:

   ```bash
   task health    # Should pass all checks
   ```

> **Note:** Projects created from the `eap-bootstrap` template already have this layer. Skip to Step 1 if your project was bootstrapped from the template.

page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#manual-assessment-without-bootstrap]

#### Manual Assessment (without bootstrap)

If the bootstrap template is not yet applied, perform the assessment manually using the following checklist:

**Project Fingerprinting:**

| Signal | How to Check | What It Tells You |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| `docs/design/conceptual/` exists | `ls docs/design/conceptual/` | May have conceptual architecture |
| `docs/requirements/functional/` has `.feature` files | `find docs/requirements -name "*.feature"` | May have BDD specs |
| `docs/decisions/` has ADR files | `ls docs/decisions/ADR-*.md` | May have architecture decisions |
| `.feature` files anywhere in repo | `find . -name "*.feature"` | BDD exists but may not be canonical |
| Architecture content in README | Search for "Architecture" heading | Has design intent, needs extraction |
| `.specify/memory/constitution.md` exists | `ls .specify/memory/` | Project started with GitHub Spec Kit core — contains governing principles, not conceptual architecture; candidate seed for Stage 8 (ADR content) only, per the Transformation Guide below |
| `.specify/memory/architecture.md` exists | `ls .specify/memory/` | Project used the community Workflow Preset extension (`spec-kit-workflow-preset`) — distinct from Spec Kit core; candidate seed for Stage 6 |
| `.kiro/specs/` exists | `ls .kiro/specs/` | Project has AWS Kiro spec artifacts — `requirements.md` is a candidate seed for Stage 7; `design.md` is a candidate seed for Stage 8 |
| `.kiro/steering/` exists | `ls .kiro/steering/` | Project has AWS Kiro steering context — candidate seed for Stage 8 (design/governance context) |
| `prd.md` exists alongside `.bmad-core/` | `ls .bmad-core/ 2>/dev/null && ls prd.md` | Project started with BMAD-METHOD — candidate seed for Stage 7 (FR specs) only; a bare `prd.md` without `.bmad-core/` is not BMAD-specific evidence |
| `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` exists alongside `.bmad-core/` | `ls .bmad-core/ 2>/dev/null && ls ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` | Project started with BMAD-METHOD — candidate seed for Stages 6 and 8 (per the Transformation Guide below); a bare `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` without `.bmad-core/` is not BMAD-specific evidence |

**Stage-by-Stage Checklist:**

| Stage | Key Question | Satisfied When |
|-------|-------------|---------------|
| 1-5 (RE) | Is the existing codebase well-understood? | Domain capabilities documented, or SMEs available |
| 6 (Conceptual) | Are bounded contexts defined? | Named BCs with glossary and context map |
| 7 (FR specs) | Do testable Gherkin scenarios exist? | `.feature` files with `@FR-*` tags in canonical location |
| 8 (Logical) | Do ADRs and technical design exist? | ADRs with canonical metadata, tech-spec constraints |
| 9 (NFR specs) | Are quality attributes specified as scenarios? | `.feature` files with `@NFR-*` tags |
| 10 (Export) | Are work items generated from specs? | GitHub Issues with `agent-task` label and constraint chains |
| 11 (Plan) | Is there a dependency-ordered plan? | `docs/project-plan.md` with phases and critical path |

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#step-2-interpret-the-compliance-matrix]

### Step 2: Interpret the Compliance Matrix

The gap assessment produces a compliance matrix like this:

```
| Stage | Name                    | Status    | Score | Gap Description                    |
|-------|-------------------------|-----------|-------|------------------------------------|
| 1-5   | Reverse Engineering     | Skip      | —     | SMEs available, domain understood  |
| 6     | Conceptual Architecture | Partial   | 45%   | No CRB submission, glossary incomplete |
| 7     | Functional Requirements | Missing   | 0%    | No Gherkin specs                   |
| 8     | Logical Architecture    | Partial   | 60%   | ADRs exist but non-canonical format |
| 9     | Non-Functional Reqs     | Missing   | 0%    | No NFR specs                       |
| 10    | Export to Issues        | Missing   | 0%    | No spec-derived issues             |
| 11    | Plan Sequence           | Missing   | 0%    | No dependency-ordered plan         |
```
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#interpreting-scores]

#### Interpreting Scores

| Overall Score | Classification | Recommended Approach |
|--------------|---------------|---------------------|
| 0-20% | **Heavy adoption** | Full pipeline execution from Stage 6 (or Stage 1 if RE needed) |
| 20-40% | **Moderate adoption** | Selective backfill with artifact transformation |
| 40-70% | **Light adoption** | Format transformation and gap filling |
| 70-100% | **Compliant** | Run `/eap-sdd-health-check` for ongoing maintenance |
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#step-3-execute-the-backfill-plan]

### Step 3: Execute the Backfill Plan

The backfill plan prescribes one of four actions per gap:

| Action | When to Use | Effort |
|--------|------------|--------|
| **Transform** | Existing artifact can be reformatted to canonical form | Low |
| **Augment** | Existing artifact is partial — run pipeline command with existing content as seed | Medium |
| **Generate** | No equivalent exists — run pipeline command from scratch | High |
| **Skip** | Stage is satisfied or legitimately not applicable | None |
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#execution-order]

#### Execution Order

Follow the pipeline stage order (6 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 11) with these exceptions:

- **Stage 1-5 (RE)** only if gap assessment recommends it (large codebase, no SMEs)
- **Stage 8 (Logical)** can be done in parallel with Stage 7 if the team has enough architects
- **Stage 10 (Export)** should wait until Stages 7 and 9 are at least partially satisfied
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#guided-execution-mode]

#### Guided Execution Mode

For interactive, step-by-step execution:

```bash
/eap-sdd-adopt
```

This walks through each backfill step, asking for confirmation before modifying files, generating CRB/ARB submissions, or exporting to external systems.

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#decision-1-reverse-engineering-vs-document-from-knowledge]

#### Decision 1: Reverse Engineering vs. Document-from-Knowledge

```
Is the codebase > 50k LOC?
├─ YES → Are SMEs available?
│   ├─ YES → Hybrid: /eap-disc-re-survey for inventory, SMEs for architecture
│   └─ NO  → Full RE pipeline (Stages 1-5)
└─ NO  → Are SMEs available?
    ├─ YES → Skip RE, seed /eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create with team knowledge
    └─ NO  → /eap-disc-re-survey + /eap-disc-re-extract minimum
```
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#decision-2-transform-vs-regenerate]

#### Decision 2: Transform vs. Regenerate

```
Does an existing artifact cover >60% of required content?
├─ YES → Is the format gap bridgeable with metadata addition?
│   ├─ YES → Transform in place (rename, restructure, add YAML metadata)
│   └─ NO  → Regenerate using existing content as seed input
└─ NO  → Generate from scratch via pipeline command
```
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#decision-3-incremental-vs-full-adoption]

#### Decision 3: Incremental vs. Full Adoption

```
Can the team dedicate focused adoption time?
├─ YES → Full adoption (all stages, complete compliance)
└─ NO  → What is the team's immediate goal?
    ├─ CRB/ARB submission → Minimum: Stages 6 + 8
    ├─ Traceable work items → Minimum: Stages 6 + 7 + 8 + 10
    └─ Compliance baseline → Incremental: one stage per sprint
```

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#phase-25-traceability-reconciliation-adoption-only]

#### Phase 2.5: Traceability Reconciliation (Adoption-Only)

> **Why this step exists:** `/eap-spec-fr-create` now includes adoption-aware status detection — it scans for existing code and suggests `implemented` or `verified` status when a match is found. However, the automated detection uses a confidence threshold and may conservatively default to `specified` when uncertain. This phase validates and corrects any misclassified entries.

| Step | Action | Command | Output |
|------|--------|---------|--------|
| 2.5.1 | Review auto-detected statuses | Read `traceability.md` | Verify `implemented`/`verified` assignments are correct |
| 2.5.2 | Fix false negatives | Manual edit of `traceability.md` | Update `specified` → `implemented` where code exists but wasn't auto-detected |
| 2.5.3 | Fill Component column for any gaps | Manual edit of `traceability.md` | Component paths populated (e.g., `components/python/src/enrollment/`) |
| 2.5.4 | Fill Tests column for features with existing tests | Manual edit of `traceability.md` | Test paths populated |
| 2.5.5 | Run health check to validate | `/eap-sdd-health-check --fix` | Auto-fixes where data can be inferred |

**When is this step needed?**

- If `/eap-spec-fr-create` flagged low-confidence matches with ⚠ warnings → review those entries
- If large sections of the codebase use naming conventions that differ from the capability slugs → manual mapping required
- If the project has code in non-standard locations → auto-detection won't find it

**How to reconcile remaining gaps:**

For each `@FR-*` row in `docs/requirements/traceability.md` still showing `specified`:

1. **Check if code exists:** Search `components/*/src/<concern>/` for implementations matching the spec
2. **If implemented:** Update status to `implemented`, fill `Component` with the source path
3. **If tests exist:** Fill `Tests` with the test file path, update status to `verified`
4. **If partially implemented:** Leave as `specified` but add a note in the `Component` column indicating partial coverage

Valid status values in order: `specified` → `implemented` → `verified`

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#phase-4-operationalize-stages-10--11]

#### Phase 4: Operationalize (Stages 10 + 11)

> **Adoption consideration:** `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` generates implementation + testing + infrastructure issues for every feature file. For features with existing code (status `implemented` or `verified` in traceability), creating implementation issues is wasteful — agents would attempt to re-implement existing code. Use the decision tree below.

**Decision 4: Export Strategy for Adopted Projects**

```
Does the feature have existing code? (traceability status = implemented/verified)
├─ YES → Does the code have adequate test coverage?
│   ├─ YES → Skip export (--skip-implemented handles this automatically)
│   └─ NO  → Export testing issues only (--testing-only)
└─ NO  → Export normally (/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create)
```

| Step | Action | Command | Output |
|------|--------|---------|--------|
| 4.1a | Export issues for UN-implemented features | `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create <path>` | Full issue set (impl + test + infra) |
| 4.1b | Export testing issues for implemented features | `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create --testing-only <path>` | Testing issues only — references existing code path |
| 4.1c | Skip fully-verified features automatically | `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create --skip-implemented <path>` | Skips features where all tags have status `implemented` or `verified` |
| 4.2 | Export to ADO Stories | `/eap-decom-spec-export-boards --stories` | ADO work items with AB# links |
| 4.3 | Generate dependency-ordered plan | `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` | `docs/project-plan.md` with phases |

**Recommended combination for adoption:** `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create --skip-implemented --testing-only <concern-path>`
- Skips features that are fully verified (all tags `verified`)
- For features with status `implemented`, generates testing issues only
- Testing issues reference the existing code path so agents know where to write tests

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#effort-estimation]

### Effort Estimation

| Adoption Level | Criteria | Typical Effort |
|---------------|----------|----------------|
| **Light (Transform)** | >70% compliant, mostly format/metadata issues | 1-2 focused sessions |
| **Moderate (Augment)** | 40-70% compliant, partial artifacts exist | 3-5 sessions |
| **Heavy (Generate)** | <40% compliant, starting from scratch | 5-10 sessions (full pipeline) |
| **Mixed** | Some stages satisfied, others missing entirely | Variable — plan per stage |

A "session" is approximately 2-4 hours of focused work by an architect using AI-assisted pipeline commands.

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#profile-a-code-but-no-architecture-docs]

#### Profile A: "Code but No Architecture Docs"

**Characteristics**: Production code with tests and CI/CD, but no architecture documentation. README describes what the service does, not how it's designed.

**Assessment**: Stages 6-11 all Missing. Stages 1-5 may be recommended if codebase is large.

**Recommended Path**:

1. Apply bootstrap template (Step 0)
2. Decide RE vs. SME knowledge (Decision 1)
3. If RE: `/eap-disc-re-survey` → `/eap-disc-re-extract` → review
4. `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` — seed with README content and team knowledge
5. `/eap-spec-fr-create` — derive from existing test descriptions and acceptance criteria
6. **Phase 2.5: Reconcile traceability** — mark existing code as `implemented`, fill `Component` and `Tests` columns
7. `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` — formalize tech decisions already embedded in code
8. Export testing-only issues for implemented features (see Agentic Handoff section)
9. `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` — plan test coverage backfill order

**Estimated effort**: Heavy (5-10 sessions)
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#profile-b-architecture-docs-in-non-canonical-format]

#### Profile B: "Architecture Docs in Non-Canonical Format"

**Characteristics**: Has architecture documentation — perhaps an `ARCHITECTURE.md`, Confluence pages, or design docs — but not in pipeline format. No BDD specs. ADRs may exist in a different template.

**Assessment**: Stage 6 Partial (40-60%), Stage 8 Partial (30-50%), all others Missing.

**Recommended Path**:

1. Apply bootstrap template (Step 0)
2. Transform existing architecture docs → seed for `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create`
3. Transform existing ADRs → canonical format with metadata
4. `/eap-spec-fr-create` — derive from existing requirements docs or acceptance criteria
5. `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` — augment existing design with missing sections
6. Continue through Stages 9-11

**Estimated effort**: Moderate (3-5 sessions)
page_texts.49:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#profile-c-everything-except-bdd-specs]

#### Profile C: "Everything Except BDD Specs"

**Characteristics**: Well-documented project with conceptual architecture, ADRs, and a project plan — but no Gherkin feature files. Work items exist in ADO but weren't generated from specs.

**Assessment**: Stages 6 and 8 Partial or Satisfied, Stages 7 and 9 Missing, Stages 10-11 Partial.

**Recommended Path**:

1. Apply bootstrap template if not present (Step 0)
2. Validate Stage 6 and 8 artifacts pass `/eap-sdd-health-check`
3. `/eap-spec-fr-create` — decompose existing capabilities into Gherkin scenarios
4. `/eap-spec-nfr-create` — derive from existing SLA docs and performance tests
5. **Phase 2.5: Reconcile traceability** — code exists but has no spec backing; update status to `implemented` for features that match existing code
6. Selective export — for implemented features, export testing issues only; for unimplemented gaps, export full issue set
7. `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` — rebuild plan from spec dependencies

**Estimated effort**: Moderate (3-5 sessions)
page_texts.50:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#profile-d-early-pipeline-adopter]

#### Profile D: "Early Pipeline Adopter"

**Characteristics**: Project used an earlier version of the pipeline. Has some canonical artifacts but is missing newer requirements (tech-spec constraints, NFR behavioral specs, traceability matrix).

**Assessment**: Most stages Partial (50-80%). Specific gaps in newer pipeline features.

**Recommended Path**:

1. Sync bootstrap template to latest version (`/eap-bootstrap-sync`)
2. Run `/eap-sdd-adopt --report-only` to identify specific gaps
3. Address gaps stage by stage (typically augment, not generate)
4. Run `/eap-sdd-health-check` to confirm compliance

**Estimated effort**: Light (1-2 sessions)
page_texts.51:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#profile-e-started-with-an-external-spec-driven-development-framework]

#### Profile E: "Started with an External Spec-Driven Development Framework"

**Characteristics**: Project began life under GitHub Spec Kit (`.specify/memory/`), AWS Kiro (`.kiro/specs/`, `.kiro/steering/`), or BMAD-METHOD (`prd.md`, `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` alongside `.bmad-core/`) before being brought onto the enterprise accelerator. Durable principles, architecture intent, and requirements already exist — just in a different framework's shape, not a canonical one.

**Assessment**: Derive the assessment from the specific artifacts the fingerprinting table above actually detects, not from the profile as a whole — a project is not assumed to have every framework's artifact just because it matches this profile. Typical patterns per detected signal: Stage 8 Partial when `constitution.md` is detected (ADR content exists but not as discrete ADRs); Stage 6 Partial when `architecture.md` or `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` is detected (conceptual/logical intent exists but not in canonical form); Stage 7 Partial when `.kiro/specs/requirements.md` or a BMAD `prd.md` is detected (specs exist but not as Gherkin); Stage 8 Partial when `.kiro/specs/design.md` is detected. A project with only one of these artifacts should score Partial on only the stage(s) that artifact seeds — not on every stage this profile lists.

**Recommended Path**:

1. Apply bootstrap template (Step 0)
2. Run `/eap-sdd-adopt --report-only` — Phase 1 fingerprinting detects the external framework's artifacts automatically (see updated fingerprinting table above)
3. Treat detected constitution/PRD/architecture content as candidate seeds, not ratified fact — route through `/architect` (Stage 6/8) and `/business-analyst` (Stage 7) for review before promoting to ADRs or `.feature` files
4. Continue the standard backfill plan for remaining gaps
5. Once compliant, run `/eap-sdd-align` to project the resulting ADRs/specs back outward as framework-specific redirects — closing the loop so the project is discoverable both to its original framework's conventions and to the canonical pipeline

**Estimated effort**: Moderate (3-5 sessions), lighter than Profile A/B since the external framework's artifacts are usually more structured than raw README prose

**See also**: [Spec-Driven Development: Industry Convergence and Gainwell's Composite Framework](../../../white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md) for the full landscape survey of these external frameworks and why Gainwell's canonical model diverges from each of them

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#artifact-transformation-guide]

### Artifact Transformation Guide

When existing artifacts can be reused, apply these transformations:

| Existing Artifact | Target Format | Transformation Steps |
|-------------------|--------------|---------------------|
| README "Architecture" section | `docs/design/conceptual/` | Extract bounded contexts, create glossary terms, generate context map |
| Confluence design pages | `docs/design/logical/` | Export to Markdown, restructure into 11-section logical doc template |
| Ad-hoc ADRs | `docs/decisions/ADR-NNN.md` | Add YAML metadata block, map to canonical status values, link to requirements |
| User stories in ADO | `.feature` files | Extract acceptance criteria → Given/When/Then, add `@FR-*` tags |
| Jest/pytest test names | Scenario candidates | Map `describe`/`it` → Feature/Scenario, validate with BA |
| SLA documents | NFR `.feature` files | Extract thresholds → `@NFR-*` tagged scenarios |
| Load test configs (k6, JMeter) | NFR performance scenarios | Map test assertions → Then clauses |
| OpenAPI specs | Structural contracts | Reference from tech-specs, validate against ADR constraints |
| Draw.io/Mermaid diagrams | Reuse directly | Move to canonical location, reference from design docs |
| Spec Kit's `.specify/memory/constitution.md` | Candidate ADR content | One article/principle at a time, review via `/architect` before ratifying |
| Workflow Preset's `.specify/memory/architecture.md` or Spec Kit core's `specs/*/spec.md` | `docs/design/conceptual/` or `.feature` files | Seed for `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` (architecture.md, from community Workflow Preset) or `/eap-spec-fr-create` (spec.md, already structured as user stories) |
| Kiro's `.kiro/specs/*/requirements.md` + `design.md` | `.feature` files + `docs/design/logical/` | Seed for `/eap-spec-fr-create` and `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` |
| Kiro's `.kiro/steering/` | Candidate ADR content | Seed for `/architect`-reviewed governance decisions |
| BMAD-METHOD's `prd.md` | `.feature` files | Seed for `/eap-spec-fr-create`, extracting acceptance criteria |
| BMAD-METHOD's `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` | `docs/design/` + candidate ADRs | Seed for `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` and `/eap-decom-logical-arch-create` |

### Agentic Handoff for Adopted Projects

The standard pipeline produces GitHub Issues that AI agents pick up for implementation. For adopted projects with existing code, the agentic handoff works differently:

[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#standard-pipeline-greenfield]

#### Standard Pipeline (Greenfield)


page_texts.56:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#how-the-handoff-differs]

#### How the Handoff Differs

| Pipeline Step | Greenfield | Brownfield (Adoption) |
|--------------|-----------|----------------------|
| `/eap-spec-fr-create` | Creates specs, status = `specified` | Creates specs retroactively, status must be manually updated to `implemented` |
| `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` | Full issue set (impl + test + infra) | **Testing-only** for implemented features; full set only for gaps |
| Agent dispatch | Agents implement from scratch | Agents write **tests for existing code** and fill coverage gaps |
| Traceability update | Automated as agents complete work | Partially manual — reconciliation required (Phase 2.5) |
| `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` | Plans full implementation order | Plans **test coverage backfill** order for existing code |
page_texts.57:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#practical-workflow]

#### Practical Workflow

1. **After retroactive spec creation** (Phase 2): `/eap-spec-fr-create` auto-detects existing code and sets traceability status to `implemented` or `verified`. Review Phase 2.5 for any low-confidence entries.
2. **At export time** (Phase 4): Run `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --create --skip-implemented --testing-only <concern>` to generate only testing issues for implemented features.
3. **Agent assignment**: Testing agents receive issues with an `Existing implementation: components/<target>/src/<concern>/` constraint pointing directly to the code they need to test.
4. **No phantom issues**: `--skip-implemented` prevents creation of implementation issues for code that already exists. `--testing-only` ensures only test-writing work is dispatched.
page_texts.58:
[strategy/guidance/processes/adoption/GUID-GOV-PROC-012-architecture-pipeline-adoption-guide.md#what-gets-exported-for-each-scenario]

#### What Gets Exported for Each Scenario

| Feature Status | Implementation Issue | Testing Issue | Infrastructure Issue |
|---------------|---------------------|--------------|---------------------|
| `specified` (no code) | YES — full constraints | YES — after impl | YES — if infra needed |
| `implemented` (code exists, no tests) | NO — suppressed by `--testing-only` | YES — primary value of adoption | Maybe — assess infra gaps separately |
| `verified` (code + tests exist) | NO — suppressed by `--skip-implemented` | NO — suppressed by `--skip-implemented` | Maybe — assess infra gaps separately |

- No Gherkin specs

| 1-5 | Skip | — | SMEs available, 35k LOC manageable |
| 6 | Partial | 50% | README has implicit BCs, no formal decomposition |
| 7 | Missing | 0% | No Gherkin specs — derive from test names + stories |
| 8 | Partial | 40% | ADRs exist but non-canonical, no tech-specs |
| 9 | Missing | 0% | No NFR specs — derive from SLA doc |
| 10 | Missing | 10% | ADO stories exist but no constraint chains |
| 11 | Missing | 0% | No dependency-ordered plan |

**Backfill Plan**: Moderate adoption (4 sessions estimated)

### Risk Management

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
|--------------|-----------------|-------------|--------|-------------------|
| Incomplete transformation | Existing artifacts lose content during format migration | Medium | High | Diff-review all transformations before committing; preserve originals in a `_legacy/` branch |
| Scope creep | Adoption expands into full redesign instead of compliance alignment | Medium | Medium | Decision 3 (incremental adoption); strict scope boundaries per stage |
| Team resistance | Engineers view adoption as overhead with no immediate value | Low | High | Start with Stage 10 (issue export) to demonstrate immediate traceability value |
| Stale artifacts | Adopted artifacts become outdated because team doesn't use pipeline commands going forward | Medium | Medium | After adoption, hand off to GUID-GOV-PROC-011 (operational runbook) for ongoing maintenance |
